profiles.name: DREADFUL
profiles.profile: This is the kind of file that makes pars look charitable. DREADFUL can sneak a decent hole or two out of the bag, but the bigger picture is a full-on demolition job: approach play keeps leaking, the putter keeps missing the bucket, and the chip game has been known to join the mutiny. The weird part is the golf occasionally flashes like it wants to behave, then immediately faceplants in the bunker or from five feet. Strong-trend evidence says this isn’t a bad stretch; it’s the identity. The only thing more consistent than the damage is the aftermath.

profiles.name: MashedBROtato
profiles.profile: MashedBROtato is the classic “how the hell is this guy still in the mix?” file. The tee ball can absolutely show up, and when the irons and putter decide to cooperate, he can bully a card into respectability. But the baseline is volatile: one week the short game rescues the mess, the next week the approach play detonates and the whole round goes sideways. This profile has enough strong evidence to say the engine is real, but the steering wheel is made of wet cardboard. When it’s on, it’s fun; when it isn’t, it’s a bar fight with a scorecard.

profiles.name: TEV_11
profiles.profile: TEV_11 is a weird one: enough tee pop to look dangerous, enough short-game touch to keep the corpse from smelling too bad, and then the irons come in like they’re actively trying to ruin the night. That’s the recurring vibe here — not total collapse, more like one giant department keeps punching holes in the floor while the rest of the bag works overtime. The evidence is enough to call it a real profile, not a fluke. If the approach play ever stops dragging the whole operation behind the truck, this thing gets a lot less ugly in a hurry.

profiles.name: Leroy4522
profiles.profile: Leroy4522 keeps finding new and creative ways to turn decent tee shots into a long day. The driver can be fine, the putter can occasionally mind its manners, but the approach game is the recurring wrecking ball and it drags the whole bag into the swamp. There’s enough evidence here to say this isn’t random bad luck; it’s the same movie with different golf courses. Every now and then a good tee day or a hot putter sneaks through, but the iron play keeps showing up like it owes the rest of the card money. Brutal, repetitive, and somehow still not boring.

profiles.name: Jakobm90
profiles.profile: There’s not much film here yet, but the one appearance was a proper shambles in the places that matter. The tee ball got bullied around, the putter didn’t save the day, and the round spent most of its time trying not to get worse. The odd wrinkle is that the approach numbers were the lone bright spot, which means the bag has at least one functioning department hiding in the wreckage. It’s way too early to stamp a final story on this file, but the first read is clear: the miss pattern is loud, ugly, and very much in charge.

profiles.name: graycrum
profiles.profile: graycrum is a tidy little contradiction. The short game and putter have been doing enough to make the card look salvageable, and there’s real evidence of a player who can scramble and score when the rest of the bag isn’t actively on fire. The catch is the irons keep showing up as the unwanted guest at the party, and that keeps turning solid patches into missed chances. This isn’t a total wreck — there’s useful golf in there — but the profile is mixed enough that every clean stretch feels one bad approach away from getting mugged.
